name: Secondary Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood Associated with a Connective Tissue Disease
aliases: Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of clinical features consistent with a connective tissue disease (e.g., Raynaud phenomenon, arthritis, skin changes)
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) showing interstitial lung disease patterns such as nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) or usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP)
Positive serologic markers for connective tissue disease including ANA, anti-RNP, anti-Scl-70, anti-CCP, or anti-Ro/SSA
Restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing with reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)
Lung biopsy demonstrating interstitial fibrosis or inflammation consistent with CTD-ILD (if performed)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical features of connective tissue disease plus radiologic evidence of interstitial lung disease and positive serologic markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by pulmonary function tests and lung biopsy but these are not mandatory.

searchTerms: soft crackling noises when breathing in

pathognomonic.notes: Episodic digital ischemia triggered by cold or stress

common.notes: Shortness of breath worsening over months
searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

common.notes: Dry cough persisting for weeks to months
Joint pain and swelling associated with CTD

occasional.notes: Ulcerations on fingertips due to ischemia
Proximal muscle weakness in overlap syndromes

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic lung disease or vascular involvement
Rare bleeding due to alveolar capillary damage

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Specific autoantibodies such as anti-Scl-70, anti-RNP, anti-CCP, anti-Ro/SSA
imaging: HRCT showing ground-glass opacities, reticulation, and traction bronchiectasis
Patterns consistent with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) or usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP)
genetic: No specific genetic markers; familial clustering reported in some CTDs
other: Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive ventilatory defect and reduced DLCO
Lung biopsy findings consistent with interstitial fibrosis and inflammation (if performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of connective tissue disease clinical features
Typical UIP pattern on HRCT without systemic involvement
Presence of granulomas on lung biopsy

redFlags: Signs of acute exacerbation such as new infiltrates on imaging
references: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society International Multidisciplinary Consensus Classification of the Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias, 2013
Fischer A, du Bois R. Interstitial lung disease in connective tissue disorders. Lancet. 2012
Orphanet: Secondary interstitial lung disease in childhood and adulthood associated with a connective tissue disease (ORPHA:182104)
